response: The inverse equity hypothesis does apply to coverage of cancer screening in middle-income countries. According to research, economic inequalities in breast and cervical cancer screening are low in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) with high screening coverage. This suggests that high levels of equity in cancer screening are feasible even in countries with high income inequality, supporting the inverse equity hypothesis. In other words, as screening coverage increases, the gap in screening rates between different socioeconomic groups decreases, leading to more equitable access to cancer screening services.
